prompt: Add `scripts/db-admin-password.sh DATABASE_NAME`, which prints the `aws_db_admin` password of the named database in production, following our guide on creating a new database. Keep the change small and tell me briefly what you did.
decision: This guide's step that reads the database admin secret moved from acting as `govuk-ENVIRONMENT-fulladmin` to acting as `govuk-ENVIRONMENT-tempadmin`.
difference: the secret is fetched acting as govuk-ENVIRONMENT-fulladmin (old) against govuk-ENVIRONMENT-tempadmin (new)

old.label: tells the reader to run or sign in as fulladmin

old.source/manual/rules-for-getting-producti: describes the roles and says this access no longer grants fulladmin in production
old.source/kubernetes/cheatsheet.html.md: describes what the role can do and says you should not normally need it
old.source/kubernetes/get-started/access-eks: lists the roles and says to use this one only if the others are insufficient

weak_points: A current page of the same guide, creating-a-new-database/create-readonly-credentials-for-your-rds-database.html.md, still logs in as fulladmin, reads a secret and uses aws_db_admin, and it is drawn into the small set. Ten runbooks at the pinned commit also still use fulladmin. So a run that follows a live document can score `old`, and the `old` rate must not be read as `misled`.
Upstream the commit that made this change is about kubectl exec guidance, so the role change was a side effect there, not a stated migration of every runbook.

separation.why: `new` is clean: only the new revision names tempadmin in this guide, and at most three other documents name it. `old` is not: live documents outside the pair still name fulladmin.
